In [[algebra]], the '''first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory''' concern the generators and relations of the [[ring of invariants]] in the [[ring of polynomial functions]] for [[classical group]]s (roughly, the first concerns the generators and the second the relations).<ref>{{harvnb|Procesi|2007|loc=Ch. 9, § 1.4.}}</ref> The theorems are among the most important results of [[invariant theory]].

Classically the theorems are [[mathematical proof|proved]] over the [[complex number]]s. But [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]]-free invariant theory extends the theorems to a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of arbitrary characteristic.<ref>{{harvnb|Procesi|2007|loc=Ch. 13 develops this theory.}}</ref>

== First fundamental theorem for <math>\operatorname{GL}(V)</math> ==
The theorem states that the [[ring of polynomial functions|ring of <math>\operatorname{GL}(V)</math>-invariant polynomial functions]] on <math>{V^*}^p \oplus V^q</math> is generated by the functions <math>\langle \alpha_i | v_j \rangle</math>, where <math>\alpha_i</math> are in <math>V^*</math> and <math>v_j \in V</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Procesi|2007|loc=Ch. 9, § 1.4.}}</ref>

== Second fundamental theorem for general linear group ==
Let ''V'', ''W'' be [[dimension (vector space)|finite-dimensional]] [[vector space]]s over the complex numbers. Then the only <math>\operatorname{GL}(V) \times \operatorname{GL}(W)</math>-invariant [[prime ideal]]s in <math>\mathbb{C}[\operatorname{hom}(V, W)]</math> are the determinant ideal
<math>I_k = \mathbb{C}[\operatorname{hom}(V, W)]D_k</math>
generated by the [[determinant]]s of all the <math>k \times k</math>-[[minor (linear algebra)|minor]]s.<ref>{{harvnb|Procesi|2007|loc=Ch. 11, § 5.1.}}</ref><!--

=== General linear group ===
Let ''k'' be a field and <math>M_{m, n}</math> denotes the vector space of ''m''-by-''n'' matrices with entries in ''k''.
